newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-ENGLISH CLUBS SET TO WELCOME OVERSEAS STARS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ENGLISH CLUBS SET TO WELCOME OVERSEAS STARS.

text.p: A rise in the number of overseas players in English club rugby looks certain following a decision by the Rugby Football Union (RFU) on Friday to rewrite the qualification rules for league matches.

The RFU committee announced they were scrapping the six-month qualification rule for overseas players not contracted to their home unions, with All Black forwards Zinzan Brooke and Michael Jones tipped to be the first new arrivals.
Neither are currently tied to the New Zealand Rugby Union, and have been the subject of interest from Harlequins who have already signed French pair Laurent Cabannes and Laurent Benezech.
Although each club is restricted to a maximum of two non-European players in a competitive match, Harlequins' former England coach Dick Best predicted a massive influx.

"It is open doors," he said. "You will now see the biggest influx of players the game has ever known. Every club that can afford it will have their two men from overseas. Zinzan Brooke and Michael Jones are ideal candidates.
"It may be that players coming towards the end of their careers and out of contract with their own unions will be the only ones available, but British clubs must choose the player and not the age."
Players who are contracted to non-European nations must still serve a 180-day residential qualification.
